questions.q: According to the lesson, what do Consultant interviews primarily test, compared to Administrator and Developer interviews?
options: Communication and judgment in client conversations, with technical depth as secondary
Apex syntax memorization
Typing speed during a live demo
Knowledge of Salesforce's internal server architecture
questions.explain: The lesson states that while technical depth still matters, communication and judgment in handling client conversations are the main focus of Consultant interviews.

questions.q: In the structured answer the lesson gives for "how do you gather requirements," what comes before documenting requirements?
options: Signing the contract
Writing the Apex code
Scheduling the certification exam
Identifying stakeholders and running discovery workshops
questions.explain: The lesson's structured process starts with identifying stakeholders and running discovery sessions before documentation and prioritization happen.

questions.q: When a stakeholder isn't sure what they need, what does the lesson say the interview is testing?
options: Whether you can guess correctly on the first try
Whether you escalate immediately to a manager
Whether you ask good clarifying questions and guide them toward clarity
Whether you can write a validation rule on the spot
questions.explain: The lesson frames this scenario as testing whether the candidate can ask clarifying questions rather than guess.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend when a non-technical stakeholder is involved in discovery?
options: Insist they learn Salesforce terminology before the meeting continues
Focus on understanding their business process first, then translate it into Salesforce concepts yourself
Skip the meeting and work only from written notes
Hand them a glossary of object and field names
questions.explain: The lesson advises understanding the business process first and doing the translation work yourself, rather than requiring the stakeholder to think in platform terms.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say simply telling a client "that's against best practice" is a weaker answer than explaining the tradeoff?
options: Because it reads as rigid rather than expert, compared to explaining the downside in terms the client cares about and offering an alternative
Because best practices don't actually matter in consulting
Because clients are never allowed to hear the phrase "best practice"
Because it's technically inaccurate in every case
questions.explain: The lesson explains that translating the tradeoff into client-relevant terms and offering an alternative demonstrates expertise, while a bare rejection does not.
